text: In nineteen eighty-two, a truck driver flew sixteen thousand feet into the sky. In a lawn chair.
Larry had wanted to fly his whole life, but his eyesight was too poor to become a pilot.
So in his backyard in California, he tied forty-two weather balloons to a garden chair.
He packed sandwiches, a soda, a radio, and a pellet gun.
The plan was simple: drift gently over the desert, then pop a few balloons to come back down.
Then the cord tying his chair to his Jeep snapped.
He didn't drift up gently. He shot up like a cork.
One thousand feet. Five thousand. Sixteen thousand, freezing cold, right in the airspace of a busy airport, where two airliners reported a man in a lawn chair.
Larry shot a few balloons, started sinking, and then dropped the gun.
Luckily, he'd already popped enough to come down.
Unluckily, he came down right onto a power line.
Here's why he went up so fast. Ever tried to hold a beach ball under water? The water shoves it back up.
Air does the same thing to helium. Forty-two beach balls, all pushing up at once.
The aviation authority fined him fifteen hundred dollars, but had to drop one charge, because there is no licence for flying a lawn chair.
Today that chair sits in the National Air and Space Museum, next to real aircraft.
